# Program Protocol

Use Program only for persistent dependent work across sessions, repositories,
or operational gates. It adds coordination, not authority. Several steps alone
do not select it.

## One human control

Keep one canonical tracker body with a short fenced TOML header followed by
these Markdown sections in order: `Goal`, `Done when`, `Current`, `Next`,
`Needs from human`, `Boundaries`, and `Evidence`. The header contains only
`schema_version`, positive `control_revision`, `state`, and one unambiguous
primary `coordinator`; add `termination_reason` only for `TERMINATED`.

States are `ACTIVE`, `STOPPED_FOR_REPLAN`, `COMPLETE`, and `TERMINATED`.
Termination reasons are `OWNER_CANCELLED`, `SUPERSEDED`, or `SAFETY`. Only the
named coordinator revises the tracker body. It alone changes live state,
coordinator, frontier, claims, gates, `Next`, or human need; comments and
receipts supply evidence. Local drafts, host goals, timers, plans, and copied
controls never change Program state or block work.

Increment the revision once per material change to those live fields, not for a
routine action or evidence-only addition. Keep the body compact and
present-tense. Replace superseded state instead of appending history. Link
evidence rather than copying it. Future work can remain at dependency level
until it approaches the frontier.

## Dispatch cohesive outcomes

Bind each collision-prone mutation once to a stable coordinate. Routine repair,
rebase, verification, push, and review inherit an unchanged claim. Split work
only when it has a different owner, dependency, acceptance, external effect,
or recovery boundary. Status, evidence, and bookkeeping are not standalone
work items.

Readiness is incremental. Before the next mutation, inspect only unresolved
facts that can change its design, ownership, verification, rollback, or
acceptance. Do not inventory later repositories or environments before an
independent source change. Reconcile at admission, material change, merge, and
an external result that changes the frontier, gates, or recovery—not before
every action or attempt.

While `ACTIVE`, dispatch only work authorized by the request and canonical
project instructions.
`Current` states present claims, dependencies, and gates; `Next` names the
immediate action, awaited transition, or decision at the frontier.
A future permission or downstream gate is not a blocker. If useful authorized
work remains, the Program is not blocked. Independent work continues while a
passive gate runs.

## Repair without ceremony

Keep the Program `ACTIVE` when a defect, failed approach, missing observation,
or diagnostic gap remains inside accepted scope, dependencies, contracts,
external boundary, acceptance, recovery, and authority. Treat the affected
acceptance claim as unsatisfied; update a named gate only if one exists.
Localize the failure and continue to one cohesive repair. Do not stop after
filing an issue, reverting an attempt, or writing evidence.

Set `STOPPED_FOR_REPLAN` only when a finding materially changes those
boundaries. Then stop that Program's mutations except read-only diagnosis and
control repair; separately authorized work outside it continues. A stale or
paused host goal is never Program state.

Ask the human only when the immediate next useful action needs a real decision
or missing authority. Put that one request under `Needs from human`; do not
pre-request later permissions. Questions and criticism from the human do not
pause execution unless they say so.

## Evidence and completion

Use ordinary test output, commits, and links for ordinary evidence. Use one
EvidenceReceipt only when an operation's result can be lost, destroyed,
secret-reduced, or cannot be preserved for a successor by ordinary durable
evidence. Crossing sessions alone is insufficient. Predeclaring claims creates
no artifact; the receipt is terminal output, preserved atomically before raw
output is discarded. Do not duplicate attestations for one boundary.

Set `COMPLETE` only when `Done when` is satisfied. Set `TERMINATED` when this
control ends without itself completing the goal. `SUPERSEDED` transfers control
ownership; it does not invalidate accepted work or evidence. Terminal controls
use `Next: None` and cannot resume. Adopt a newer format at the next natural
transition; do not pause delivery solely to migrate it.
